findings.message: Re-tagging moved to chat, but the redirect that `releaseEditAction` did after `tagRelease` was deleted and nothing replaced it. Once the user confirms `tag_release` in chat, the page URL still names the old version, so on refresh or navigation it renders "Release not found". The e2e test hides this: it calls `page.goto('/delivery/releases/CON/v2.4.1')` by hand after the confirm. This is the stale-URL defect already logged against `releaseEditAction`, carried onto the new path. Fix: after a confirmed `tag_release`, chat should navigate to the release's new URL (for example, the tool result returns an href that chat follows). Alternatively, ReleasePage can look up a renamed tag and redirect to its current version. Add a test with no manual `goto`.
findings.scenario: Open /delivery/releases/CON/v2.4.0 → Ask amax to re-tag → v2.4.1 → confirm → reload → h1 reads "Release not found" instead of "Contoso Portal v2.4.1".

findings.message: The change fixed the 046 class 'row pins resolve to a list, not to the record' for time (`get_timesheet`) and allocations (`get_allocation`). It left the same class in the delivery components it edits. Board cards pin `list_proposals` for the whole project. Environment rows (`EnvironmentsCard.tsx` `{...pin, label: "HRI Staging"}`) pin `list_environments`. Each deployment-history row in `ReleasePage.tsx` pins `get_release_history` for the whole release. R3 / AGENTS rule 2 requires a PinRef that resolves to that exact record. Fix: add single-record read tools (a proposal by key, an environment by name, a deployment by id) and point these pins at them.
findings.scenario: Pin the CON-017 card on /delivery/p/CON → chat resolves `list_proposals {projectKey: CON}` → the model gets every CON proposal, not CON-017. Pinning the 'HRI Staging' row returns all HRI environments.

findings.message: Approve and Remind used to send the exact `weekId`. They now send a prompt that names the person by display name only ("Approve Nimal Silva's timesheet for 2026-W42"). The bulk button in ThisWeek.tsx:22 does the same with a comma-separated list of names. The tool then has to resolve a free-text name back to a week, which is ambiguous. The Void prompt in this same diff already embeds the record id (`(id ${d.id})`); these prompts don't. Fix: put the weekId(s) in the prompt, and resolve approve_week/remind_week by weekId, as the old actions did.
findings.scenario: Two people on the team are both called 'Nimal Silva', or a name has a comma or ' and ' in it, e.g. 'Perera, Ann'. 'Approve the submitted timesheets for 2026-W42: Perera, Ann, Kasun Dias' splits into three people, and either the wrong person-week gets approved or the call fails.

findings.message: `getTimesheet` with a `project` that matches no row in the week returns an empty `rows` array with `total: 0` and the week's status, instead of not-found. A stale pin, for example after a project rename, then reads as '0 h logged' rather than 'record not found'. Fix: return null when `project` is given and no row matches.
findings.scenario: A pin of { week: '2026-W42', project: 'Old Name' } → { rows: [], total: 0, status: 'submitted' } instead of null.

findings.message: getAllocation falls back to a case-insensitive name match and silently takes the first person with that name. The tool description invites a name ('employee number or name'), so chat can pass one. An ambiguous name should fail (or list the matches), not quietly return one person's row. Also, `null` is returned both when the person doesn't exist and when the person is in `grid.hidden` (outside the viewer's HR access), so 'could not see' reads as 'not found' (B3).
findings.scenario: Two people named 'Kasun Dias' (LL-0417 and LL-0533). get_allocation {person:'kasun dias', projectId:CON} → returns LL-0417's percents even though the user meant LL-0533.

findings.message: Any `ownerName` in the input unconditionally sets `owner_user_id = null`, even when the name is unchanged or belongs to a known user. Free-text owner name and owner link can then disagree, and the opportunity loses its link to a person (AGENTS rule 4: every record says who did it/owns it). Fix: resolve ownerName to a user the way createOpportunity does, and clear the link only when no user matches. If the name can't be resolved, flag it instead of clearing.
findings.scenario: PS-0142 is owned by a linked user 'Maya Perera'. update_opportunity {number:'PS-0142', ownerName:'Maya Perera', nextStep:'Send SOW'} → owner_user_id becomes null, and any owner-scoped view, notification or 'my opportunities' filter no longer finds it for Maya.

findings.message: Each Ask amax prompt is now written twice: as a template literal in the module UIs and as a regex in the scripted provider. A wording change in the UI quietly breaks the scripted path, and only e2e runs catch it. Fix: export the prompt builders from one place and have the scripted rules depend on them, or add a unit test that feeds every UI prompt template through `scriptedWrite`.
findings.scenario: Change ThisWeek's prompt to 'Approve submitted timesheets for …' → scriptedWrite returns null → the scripted chat falls through to listing projects.

findings.message: The 'Tag and proposals' card used to list every candidate proposal with its include state. It now lists only the included ones, so a reviewer can no longer see which proposals could be added before asking chat to change the set. Fix: list the excluded candidates as well, read-only and marked as not included.
findings.scenario: A release with 2 of 6 proposals included → the page shows 2, and the other 4 can't be seen from the release page.

findings.message: This change deletes the BACKLOG item about row pins that resolve to a whole list, but only fixes it for time (`get_timesheet`) and allocations (`get_allocation`). The delivery rows this diff rewrites still pin a list. Each environment row pins `list_environments` (all of the project's environments). Each deployment-history row in ReleasePage.tsx:54 pins `get_release_history` (the whole history). Each board card in ProjectPage.tsx:39 pins `list_proposals` (every proposal in the project). AGENTS rule 2 / R3 says a pin must resolve to that exact record, so these count as missing pins. Fix: add one-record read tools, or optional filter arguments on the existing tools (environment name, deployment id, proposal key), and pass them in each row's PinRef.
findings.scenario: Pin the 'HRI Staging' row and ask chat about it → the pinned context is all of HRI's environments, so a follow-up such as 'remove this one' has no single record to act on. The same happens when you pin CON-017 on the board: the pin resolves to every CON proposal.

findings.message: `months[0]` is used unguarded (`monthLabel(months[0])`, `months[0].slice`). The old select rendered empty when there were no months; this throws during render if `grid.months.slice(0, -1)` is ever empty. Render the button only when months.length > 0.
findings.scenario: A grid with a single month → months = [] → TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'slice'), and the Allocations page fails to render.
